# Compare grids without changing the time question

[Hold the timestep fixed. Compare the same physical Fourier modes.]{.lesson-deck}
:::

The [vorticity lesson](../vorticity/index.qmd) starts with an exact vortex.
Here the retained spatial-refinement driver uses a nonlinear double-shear
field on the **unit square**. There is no supplied exact solution at later
times. The finest grid supplies a numerical comparison, and its own
accuracy remains a question to investigate.

If both grid spacing and timestep change together, a smaller difference
cannot identify which change mattered. This driver uses the same
$h=\Delta t$ on every spatial level, then repeats one level with a smaller
$h$ as a separate control.

## Build the same equation on each grid

```{.cpp include="model.cpp" snippet="setup"}
```

Only the grid size changes in the spatial ladder. Viscosity, shear-layer
parameters, timestep and observation times remain fixed. The
`SpectralCPUStack` and the same vorticity solver are composed afresh for
each resolution. Fourier resolution and spectral accuracy are discussed
in @trefethen2000; a nonlinear calculation still needs its time error
controlled separately.

The layer parameter $\rho$ describes thickness $1/\rho$ in this unit box.
Its raw cells per thickness are $N/\rho$, and the two-thirds retained
band reduces the effective resolution. A small program that finishes
successfully need not resolve that layer.

## Match integer modes and their normalization

A fine-grid field cannot simply be subtracted from a coarse-grid array.
The helper matches signed integer Fourier modes that the coarse layout
can represent, then transforms the restricted coefficients on that grid.
Because forward FFTs are unscaled, it first adjusts their scale:

$$
\widehat\omega_{\mathrm{coarse}}
=\frac{N_{\mathrm{coarse}}^2}{N_{\mathrm{fine}}^2}
\widehat\omega_{\mathrm{fine}}
$$

for each copied mode. The inverse on the coarse grid then recovers the
same physical amplitude. This is a mode-layout operation, rather than an
interpolation of all fine-grid nodal values.

```{.cpp include="../ns2d/band_error.hpp" snippet="restrict_reference" dedent=2}
```

The same restricted vorticity supplies a reference streamfunction and
velocity. The common-grid vorticity difference is measured as

$$
E_N=\sqrt{\frac{1}{N^2}\sum_{i,j}
  \bigl(\omega_N-R_N\omega_{\mathrm{ref}}\bigr)_{ij}^2},
$$

where $R_N$ denotes the implemented Fourier restriction and inverse.
The comparison includes represented coarse-grid modes; it does not
claim that the two resolutions have identical active two-thirds bands.
The CSV also records maximum vorticity difference and velocity RMS error.
Relative errors use the restricted reference norm; inspect absolute
errors when that norm vanishes, since the helper records zero in the
relative column in that case.

## Run a small ladder and a time control

From the repository root, with a compatible installed spectral CPU SDK:

```sh
mkdir -p results
openpfc compile examples/flow/spatial-refinement/model.cpp --source-root examples/flow -o results/spatial-refinement
results/spatial-refinement --resolutions 16,32 --reference 32 --dt 0.01 --times 0.02 --nu 1e-3 --rho 10 --eps 0.05 --control-n 16 --control-dt-factor 0.5 --outdir results/flow/spatial-refinement
```

This short case teaches the comparison's structure. It uses one MPI rank,
as required by this driver so every reference mode is available locally.
It preserves the existing CTest smoke configuration and the executable
name `ns2d_spatial_refine`; build users retain its original location.

The [model](model.cpp) shares
[band_error.hpp](../ns2d/band_error.hpp),
[cases.hpp](../ns2d/cases.hpp),
[vorticity_stream.hpp](../ns2d/vorticity_stream.hpp) and
[spectral.hpp](../ns2d/spectral.hpp). Keep their relative layout when
using downloaded sources; `--source-root` lets the native compiler capture
this closed group of quoted dependencies.

Inspect `spatial_errors.csv` and `run.json` below the result directory:

- `reference` identifies the finest numerical trajectory. Its zero error
  columns do not establish that it is an exact PDE solution.
- `spatial` compares a coarser run with the restricted reference at the
  same physical time and the same timestep.
- `temporal` compares two timesteps at the control grid. Their difference
  reveals sensitivity to time resolution at that grid.

`outer_rms_fraction` measures the vorticity in the outer half of the
retained band, above $N/6$ in either direction, relative to the full RMS.
It is a resolution diagnostic, not energy beyond the already masked
cutoff and not an accuracy certificate.

Increase the resolutions while holding `dt` fixed. Then lower `dt` and
repeat the whole ladder. Compare the spatial differences, time-control
difference and outer-band indicator together. Two grids and one control
pair demonstrate the workflow; they do not establish an asymptotic
convergence rate or a universal resolved-grid threshold.
